about: Residency manifest (rules-residency tech spec § 3.5). One entry per always-loaded block of a rendered fresh install. Each entry records its measured contribution (characters and lines; the template as rendered for the worst ecosystem with representative values). test/rules/residency-budget.test.js re-measures every entry, fails on a stale one, and holds the plugin-managed total to the budget below.

budget.measured_on: a rendered fresh install: CLAUDE.template.md rendered by /project-setup for each ecosystem block (worst case kept), plus every rules/*.md without paths: frontmatter; *-project.md files are user-owned and reported separately

blocks.tier: Default, with Anchor rules 3-4 marked inline
blocks.justification: The project's entry point: the tier system, the required gates, the contract trigger table and the Anchor git rules must hold from the first turn, before any task type is known.
Tier resolution decides how every other instruction binds, so it is needed before anything else is read (pre-activation); the Anchor Register is gate supremacy.
Every edit owes its gates; the terminal completion invariant and the tier table must hold before the task type is knowable (gate supremacy).
A git mutation is irreversible and outward-facing and can be asked for in any session; the prohibitions, grants and attribution rule cannot wait for a Read.
A security failure cannot wait for a Read.
Secret recording (Register #2) can happen in any code the session writes.
Scope is decided on the first finding of any review round; the frozen baseline and the fail-closed rule must precede it (pre-activation).
A first dispatch that feeds the reviewer a conclusion cannot be undone; the review is spent before any contract loads.
Capacity claims arise before any task type and must never close a gate (Register #7); compact summaries must never carry secrets (Register #2).
A correction can arrive in any session, and the redaction rule (Register #2) must bind the first record written.
The plugin user's settings, resident exactly as the user left them; outside the plugin-managed budget and never modified by the plugin.
